title: Andrew Youn's $7,000 Test With About 40 Farm Families in Bungoma
conflicts: Pilot size: 40 families (SSIR 2011, Northwestern Magazine 2007) versus 38 (Kellogg 2026, Wikipedia); story says 'about 40'. Start: January 2006 (SSIR) versus February 2006 (Wikipedia); story says 'early 2006'. Wider 2006 totals (300 from NextBillion/GOOD, 5,000 from PBS) are not used. Sequence of the winter pilot and the May 2006 full-time move reconciled as two steps, with the May decision attributed to Kellogg. What $20 a month bought differs between SSIR and Kellogg, so only the request is mentioned.
notes: Stance affirms. Co-founder John Gachunga's 2021 interview supplies the in-kind repayment detail; it is undated, so the story places the switch to cash after the first seasons. The Kellogg anniversary article and Youn's Northwestern essay are university publications and are treated as close to the founder; pivotal claims are also backed by SSIR, NextBillion, One Acre Fund or Echoing Green.
